The application seeks consent for a cold-chain logistics facility with a gross floor area of approximately 14,850 square metres. The development is proposed on a 3.2-hectare site located on the western side of Tomago Road, approximately 400 metres north of the intersection with Masonite Road. The site is zoned IN1 General Industrial under the Port Stephens Local Environmental Plan 2013 (as amended). The proposal is permissible with consent.

The key issues raised during the public exhibition period were traffic generation, noise from loading operations, light spill, and the loss of agricultural land. The report assesses these matters against the relevant provisions of the LEP and the Development Control Plan (DCP) 2018.

**2. SITE DESCRIPTION**

The subject site is currently vacant and has been used for low-intensity grazing. The land is generally level, with a slight fall from the western boundary towards Tomago Road. A drainage easement crosses the south-eastern corner of the site. Vegetation is limited to scattered remnant trees along the road frontage and a row of mature eucalypts along the western boundary.

The site is adjoined to the north by an existing transport depot, to the east by Tomago Road, and to the south and west by vacant industrial zoned land. The nearest residential properties are located approximately 600 metres to the east, in the Heatherbrae estate, separated by an intervening band of rural-residential lots.

**3. PROPOSAL DETAILS**

The proposal comprises:

Port Stephens Council council_approval_decision was approved in the resolution. Record status: current.

- A single cold storage warehouse building (14,850 m² GFA), with a maximum height of 12.5 metres to the ridge.
- Refrigerated storage chambers (approx. 9,200 m²) with a temperature range of -25°C to +4°C.
- A mezzanine level (approx. 1,100 m²) for plant and office space.
- Nine loading docks along the southern elevation, with dock levellers and canopy.
- A truck marshalling area with 14 heavy vehicle parking bays.
- 62 car parking spaces, including four accessible spaces and two electric vehicle charging stations.
- A waste enclosure, a 25,000-litre fire water tank, and a pump room.
- Landscaping along the Tomago Road frontage and the western boundary.
- Hours of operation: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week (proposed).

**4. TRAFFIC IMPACT ASSESSMENT**

A Traffic Impact Assessment (TIA) was submitted with the application, prepared by Traffic Solutions Pty Ltd, dated 12 June 2024. The TIA estimates the development will generate:

- 148 vehicle movements per day (74 in, 74 out) during the weekday peak hour.
- 96 movements during the Saturday peak hour.
- 21 heavy vehicle movements per hour during the morning peak (AM peak) and 18 per hour during the afternoon peak (PM peak).

The TIA concludes that the surrounding road network, including Tomago Road and the intersection with Masonite Road, has sufficient capacity to accommodate the additional traffic. The assessment notes that the existing intersection operates at a Level of Service (LOS) B during peak periods, and would operate at LOS C with the development in place.

The TIA recommends the following mitigation measures:

1. A left-turn deceleration lane on Tomago Road at the site access point.
2. A right-turn bay at the site access.
3. A swept path assessment for the largest articulated vehicle (19-metre B-double) be provided at detailed design stage.
4. A Construction Traffic Management Plan (CTMP) be prepared prior to the commencement of works.

documents.title: Port Stephens Council – Development Application Records
documents.content:
The application seeks consent for a cold-chain logistics facility with a gross floor area of approximately 14,850 square metres. The development is proposed on a 3.2-hectare site located on the western side of Tomago Road, approximately 400 metres north of the intersection with Masonite Road. The site is zoned IN1 General Industrial under the Port Stephens Local Environmental Plan 2013 (as amended). The proposal is permissible with consent.

The key issues raised during the public exhibition period were traffic generation, noise from loading operations, light spill, and the loss of agricultural land. The report assesses these matters against the relevant provisions of the LEP and the Development Control Plan (DCP) 2018.

**2. SITE DESCRIPTION**

The subject site is currently vacant and has been used for low-intensity grazing. The land is generally level, with a slight fall from the western boundary towards Tomago Road. A drainage easement crosses the south-eastern corner of the site. Vegetation is limited to scattered remnant trees along the road frontage and a row of mature eucalypts along the western boundary.

The site is adjoined to the north by an existing transport depot, to the east by Tomago Road, and to the south and west by vacant industrial zoned land. The nearest residential properties are located approximately 600 metres to the east, in the Heatherbrae estate, separated by an intervening band of rural-residential lots.

**3. PROPOSAL DETAILS**

The proposal comprises:

- A single cold storage warehouse building (14,850 m² GFA), with a maximum height of 12.5 metres to the ridge.
- Refrigerated storage chambers (approx. 9,200 m²) with a temperature range of -25°C to +4°C.
- A mezzanine level (approx. 1,100 m²) for plant and office space.
- Nine loading docks along the southern elevation, with dock levellers and canopy.
- A truck marshalling area with 14 heavy vehicle parking bays.
- 62 car parking spaces, including four accessible spaces and two electric vehicle charging stations.
- A waste enclosure, a 25,000-litre fire water tank, and a pump room.
- Landscaping along the Tomago Road frontage and the western boundary.
- Hours of operation: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week (proposed).

**4. TRAFFIC IMPACT ASSESSMENT**

A Traffic Impact Assessment (TIA) was submitted with the application, prepared by Traffic Solutions Pty Ltd, dated 12 June 2024. The TIA estimates the development will generate:

- 148 vehicle movements per day (74 in, 74 out) during the weekday peak hour.
- 96 movements during the Saturday peak hour.
- 21 heavy vehicle movements per hour during the morning peak (AM peak) and 18 per hour during the afternoon peak (PM peak).

The TIA concludes that the surrounding road network, including Tomago Road and the intersection with Masonite Road, has sufficient capacity to accommodate the additional traffic. The assessment notes that the existing intersection operates at a Level of Service (LOS) B during peak periods, and would operate at LOS C with the development in place.

The TIA recommends the following mitigation measures:

1. A left-turn deceleration lane on Tomago Road at the site access point.
2. A right-turn bay at the site access.
3. A swept path assessment for the largest articulated vehicle (19-metre B-double) be provided at detailed design stage.
4. A Construction Traffic Management Plan (CTMP) be prepared prior to the commencement of works.

I have reviewed the construction noise and vibration management plan submitted on 01/04/2025 (CORR-2025-058, prepared by Acoustic Solutions, dated 28/03/2025). The plan is generally consistent with the requirements of Condition 7 of the consent.

However, I note the following matters that require clarification before I can provide final sign-off:

The plan identifies sensitive receivers to the north (residential properties on Marsh Road) but does not include a specific noise monitoring protocol for these locations during the bulk earthworks phase. I would like to see a commitment to attended monitoring at the nearest receiver within the first two weeks of construction.

3. Vibration limits are cited as per BS 7385, but the plan does not reference Council's own vibration policy for heritage items. Note that the site is not within a heritage conservation area, so this may not be applicable, but please confirm.

Please advise the applicant that my review is conditional pending these clarifications. I am otherwise satisfied with the plan.
